memory_candidates.content: When adding a mechanically-diffable byte-parity assertion between two co-maintained 'twin' files (e.g. base/hard orchestrate engines), any cross-reference comment explaining the twin relationship must live in ONLY ONE of the two files (matching the existing convention where such comments live in the 'harder'/more-specific file, referencing the simpler one) -- adding the same explanatory paragraph to both breaks a literal diff-based parity test even though the underlying logic is identical. Tag such comments with a unique, greppable marker (e.g. 'HARD-MODE-TWIN-CROSS-REFERENCE') so a parity-checking script can strip exactly that line before comparing, rather than trying to normalize free-form prose.

To test a bash region extracted from a SKILL.md file that calls an external recorder/logger script via a RELATIVE path (e.g. `bash .claude/scripts/system-defect-record.sh ...`) without polluting the real repo's event log: run the test's execution subshell with cwd set to a mktemp workdir (never the repo root). The relative path then fails to resolve, the call fails, and the region's own pre-existing `|| echo "... failed (non-fatal)"` swallow-and-continue logic handles it harmlessly -- no stub or mock needed, and no real side effect occurs. This mirrors an existing convention (test-validate-handoff-location.sh deliberately omits system-defect-record.sh from its test workdir for the same reason).

When a fix needs to reset a persisted counter/budget field (e.g. cycle_count) while preserving OTHER cross-invocation fields on the SAME file (e.g. a monotonic dispatch_seq_counter that must never repeat within a task), do not reuse an existing 'archive-then-fall-through-to-fresh-init' pattern even if one already exists nearby for a superficially similar purpose (e.g. a staleness detector) -- fresh-init wipes ALL fields to defaults. Instead: archive a COPY (not a move) of the current file for auditability, then rewrite the SAME path in place from that copy with only the specific field(s) reset via a targeted jq update (`.cycle_count = 0`), leaving every other field untouched. This preserves invariants (like 'never repeats a value within a task') that a generic fresh-init would silently violate.
